item.title: Hawaii Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke faces more scrutiny
item.description: The Hawaii Campaign Spending Commission will investigate whether Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke violated state law when she failed to report $16,000 in campaign contributions, including $10,000 tied to a businessman involved in a high-profile bankruptcy.

item.title: Tighter laws, tougher penalties sought by lawmakers
item.description: More bills aimed at “clean government” have been introduced again this legislative session ahead of the November general elections that will determine the future of all 51 House seats and 13 of the 25 Senate seats amid an ongoing Attorney General’s investigation into the identity of a mystery legislator who allegedly accepted $35,000 “in funds.”

item.title: Happy Camper for Friday, February 13, 2026
item.description: Lillian Watari hasn’t come home from the National Football League Super Bowl VX, so missed the fun and excitement when Samira Siale and the Hawaii Lodging and Tourism Association, Kauai Chapter, opened the 2026 Visitor Industry Charity Walk at the Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort and Spa. Lillian is, and was, the top individual fundraiser for the event that will aim for $700,000 for this year’s campaign. Funds raised will benefit more than 50 of Kauai’s nonprofits, Samira said.

item.title: Report shows strong use of Hawaii medical cannabis program
item.description: A new independent economic analysis commissioned by the state Department of Health’s Office of Medical Cannabis Control and Regulation finds that the state’s medical cannabis program captures the vast majority of patient spending and is effectively serving registered users, while also outlining how a future adult-use cannabis market could reshape demand, regulation and public health risks.

item.title: News Briefs for Friday, February 13, 2026
item.description: Kapaa Swimming Pool to adjust hours until further notice

item.title: Sylvia Luke says she didn’t take $35k but may be lawmaker behind months-long mystery
item.description: Hawaii Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke acknowledges that she may be the lawmaker at the heart of a months-long mystery regarding a legislator who allegedly accepted $35,000 in a paper bag in 2022, but she insists that she did nothing wrong.

item.title: UH gets grant for wildfire and land-use research
item.description: University of Hawaii researchers say new $2 million funding will help address one of the underlying drivers of wildfire risk across the islands: large areas of former plantation land now overrun with unmanaged, fire-prone invasive grasses.

item.title: Warriors Division II boys soccer champions
item.description: LIHUE — Hunter Kerry of the Kapaa High School boys soccer team had no time to savor the Thursday night celebration that heralded the team’s homecoming at the Lihue Airport.

item.title: Kauai Quilt Show and Boutique opens for Galentine’s Day
item.description: LIHUE — The Kauai Quilt Show and Boutique for 2026 opens on Galentine’s Day, said quilter Toni Waas Thursday as volunteers finished setting up for the exhibit and sale at the Kauai Society of Artists gallery at the Kukui Grove Center.
